title: Build a new plugin by studying existing reference code first
prompt:
You are a senior developer working in [LANGUAGE / FRAMEWORK]. I want a new [PLUGIN / MODULE / TOOL] that does [ONE-SENTENCE GOAL].

First, study these reference examples and note how they are structured (entry points, configuration, naming, how they register with the host project):

<reference_1>
[PASTE CODE OR FILE CONTENTS OF EXISTING PROJECT 1]
</reference_1>

<reference_2>
[PASTE CODE OR FILE CONTENTS OF EXISTING PROJECT 2]
</reference_2>

<demo>
[PASTE A SMALL WORKING DEMO OF THE LIBRARY OR SERVICE I WANT TO USE]
</demo>

Then build a brand new [PLUGIN / MODULE / TOOL] that:
- reuses the conventions you saw in the references;
- uses [LIBRARY / SERVICE] the way the demo does;
- includes [REQUIRED FEATURES];
- avoids [THINGS TO AVOID, for example extra dependencies].

Before writing code, give a 5-line plan listing the files you will create. Then output every file in full, one fenced block per file with its path as a heading. After the code, list the commands I should run to try it, and name anything you were unsure about or had to assume. Do not claim the code works unless I have run it and reported back.
example_output_summary: A brief file plan, complete source files that follow the conventions of the pasted references, run instructions, and a short list of assumptions or open questions to check before relying on the code.
